Though the top bar is heavy: Step 1 header, two pills, All 2, Review and execute, plus Step 2 and Step 3 on the right. Three zones competing for the eye.

answers.R9: Yes, Full desk lets me go at my pace: left list of items, all content in view, no auto-advance. The 'Full desk is now your default' notice is a decent touch. would_turn_off: Three numbered 'Step' labels (Step 1, 2, 3) on one screen read like a wizard or a form, not a game; it is the AI-dashboard look
Right column Step 2/3 text bullets: a dense wall of small type next to the main stage
Crisis banner art is a dark gradient with a faint silhouette; looks like a placeholder, no illustration to speak of
Pill buttons everywhere (Choose, Accept, Change, All 6, Review and execute) with few visual differences between the types
Map mode terrain is blobs, nothing like Suzerain or Into the Breach map polish
clickable_confusions: Step pills (Now: Xi Jinping calls, Takaichi visits, +3 more): tab or label?
Option card: whole card or only the Choose link?
Recommended star banner: label or button
Skip this call looks like a secondary button but its sentence beside it looks like a tooltip
Guided/Full desk toggle is clear, but is Full desk reversible: the notice says yes

wording.Recommended vs Staff picks: Recommended reads clearer: one word, a star, and it names who recommends it (Secretary of State). 'Staff picks' sounds like a store curation, and 'staff' is vague next to cabinet roles. Still, 'Recommended by your advisors' in the right column and 'Recommended' on the meetings card use the same word for different things (an option vs an order you must Accept); I would call the right column 'Proposals' and keep 'Recommended' for the starred option. Also Accept and Choose are two verbs for one act.

agenda.verbatim: This is a lot clearer than a plain list and the flow is honest: it tells me what Execute will do before I press it, which most strategy games hide. The review screen is the best-crafted one. But it still looks like a form wizard: numbered steps, grey pill buttons, text cards. Frostpunk gives a laws screen with weight and art; this has copy and gradients. The consequence lines in red and green are nice. Fix the Skip button position, the pill-button monoculture and the step labels, and give the crisis card a real illustration. I would stay past five minutes, but I would not yet say it is hand-crafted.
